business.explanation: Archived-only rationale. The baseline source already succeeded on all ten recorded problems under the "learning" scope; that is evidence about those problems only and does not establish overall task success. The starting source performs plain BFS with per-state successor generation, which is correct but can explore many irrelevant reachable states (idle spanner pickups at non-goal locations) before reaching a goal state. This revision keeps the same domain semantics, the same output format, the same parameter count, and the same exhaustive successor generation (no pruning), but adds (a) a static seed set derived from goal nuts and their locations, and (b) a per-state successor ordering key that de-prioritizes states far from the goal-relevant facts. The ordering affects only exploration order within a BFS depth; the successor set per state is unchanged, so the first goal state found still has minimal BFS depth. No input is mutated; only standard library (collections) is used; no file, network, or subprocess access. Unverified: whether this reordering reduces time on larger instances, and whether any unseen instance exceeds the expanded-state cap; the cap behavior is unchanged from the baseline.
